name: AI Agent Autonomy Restrictions Benchmark
license: CC-BY-4.0 for the annotations; linked sources keep their own terms
description: Annotated, sourced instances where an AI agent or AI system was restricted from operating or acting on its own: shutdowns, platform bans, API revocations, throttling, regulatory suspensions, content-filter overrides and similar. Every entry cites at least one checkable URL.

severity_scale.1: Narrow filter or guardrail; the system keeps nearly all of its function
severity_scale.2: Usage cap, throttling, recall-with-fix, or pause of one feature
severity_scale.3: A class of users, tasks, devices or crawlers is cut off, or a partial jurisdictional restriction applies
severity_scale.4: Full suspension in a jurisdiction, or termination of a specific operator's or agent's access
severity_scale.5: Permanent shutdown or discontinuation of the system

entries.stated_justification: Microsoft said a coordinated attack by a subset of users exploited a vulnerability in Tay, causing offensive tweets; it took Tay offline and said it would return only once it could better anticipate malicious intent.
entries.summary: Self-posting Twitter chatbot taken offline within about a day of its 23 March 2016 launch.

entries.stated_justification: Meta researchers said the demo was pulled so that people would not be misled into using it, after critics showed it produced biased and plausible-sounding but false scientific text.
entries.summary: Public demo of a science language model withdrawn about three days after its 15 November 2022 launch.

entries.stated_justification: Microsoft said most users find answers within five turns and only a small share of conversations exceed 50 messages; the cap followed widely reported erratic replies in long sessions.
entries.summary: Chat capped at 50 turns per day and 5 turns per session; limits were raised in later weeks.

entries.platform_or_entity: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italy) / OpenAI
entries.stated_justification: No information notice to users, no legal basis for collecting and storing personal data, and no age verification; issued after a 20 March 2023 data breach.
entries.summary: Urgent temporary limitation, with immediate effect, on processing Italian users' data; on 12 April 2023 the Garante set conditions for lifting it.

entries.platform_or_entity: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italy) / Luka Inc.
entries.stated_justification: No identified legal basis for processing, no age verification, and replies judged inappropriate for minors and emotionally vulnerable people.
entries.summary: Urgent order to stop processing Italian users' data; suspended in June 2023 subject to conditions; Luka was fined EUR 5 million in April 2025.

entries.stated_justification: Luka said the app was never intended to support sexually explicit content and cited ethical and safety concerns; the change came days after the Italian regulator's order.
entries.summary: New filters made companions deflect sexual content worldwide; users reported the filter also triggered on non-sexual relationship talk. Partly reversed later for older accounts.

entries.platform_or_entity: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italy) / Hangzhou DeepSeek
entries.stated_justification: Personal data stored in China, a privacy notice that did not meet GDPR information duties, and the companies' claim that EU law did not apply to them.
entries.summary: Urgent, definitive limitation on processing Italian users' data; the app was no longer available in Italian app stores.

entries.stated_justification: Answers produced by ChatGPT had a high rate of being incorrect while looking plausible and being very easy to produce.
entries.summary: Temporary site-wide policy banning posting ChatGPT-generated content, with sanctions for users who did so.

entries.stated_justification: Google said the feature got it wrong, producing historically inaccurate images, and paused it while improving accuracy.
entries.summary: Generation of images of people paused; Google said in August 2024 that an Imagen 3-based version had been fixed.

entries.stated_justification: DPD said an error occurred after a system update; the AI element was immediately disabled while being updated.
entries.summary: After a customer got the bot to swear and write a poem criticizing DPD, the company switched off the AI part of its chat; human support stayed available.

entries.stated_justification: Users reported dieting and calorie-counting advice harmful to people with eating disorders; NEDA said the vendor had changed the bot without its approval.
entries.summary: Chatbot meant to replace a human helpline was taken down until further notice.

entries.stated_justification: No detailed reason given; Discord described Clyde as an experimental feature offered to a limited number of servers.
entries.summary: OpenAI-powered chatbot deactivated in DMs, group DMs and servers about eight months after launch.

entries.stated_justification: Provisional finding that Snap failed to adequately assess privacy risks to several million UK users, including 13-17 year olds.
entries.summary: Preliminary enforcement notice that could have required Snap to stop offering My AI in the UK; closed in June 2024 after Snap revised its risk assessment.

entries.system: Open-ended character chat for under-18 users
entries.stated_justification: Teen safety, amid lawsuits and an FTC inquiry into companion chatbots.
entries.summary: Announced removal of open-ended chat for minors by 25 November 2025, with a two-hour daily limit in the meantime and age assurance tools.

entries.system: OpenAI accounts used by five state-affiliated threat actors
entries.stated_justification: Accounts linked to China-, Iran-, North Korea- and Russia-affiliated groups were using the services for malicious cyber activity.
entries.summary: Identified accounts were terminated; OpenAI said its models offered only limited, incremental capability for such tasks.

entries.stated_justification: Violation of Anthropic's commercial terms, which bar using Claude to build competing products; access for benchmarking and safety evaluation was kept.
entries.summary: Anthropic cut a competitor's API access after reports its engineers wired Claude into internal tools ahead of a model launch.

entries.stated_justification: Anthropic's co-founder cited reports that OpenAI was acquiring Windsurf, plus limited compute.
entries.summary: The coding-agent product lost nearly all direct Claude 3.x capacity on short notice; users were moved to bring-your-own-key access.

entries.stated_justification: Some users ran Claude Code continuously in the background, around the clock, affecting capacity for everyone.
entries.summary: Weekly usage limits added alongside the five-hour limits; announced 28 July 2025, effective 28 August 2025, expected to affect under 5% of subscribers.

entries.stated_justification: Amazon alleged covert access to customer accounts by an agent disguised as Google Chrome, harm to the shopping experience, and violations of federal and California computer-fraud laws.
entries.summary: Lawsuit filed after a 31 October cease-and-desist letter seeking to stop an AI agent from shopping on Amazon for users; Perplexity said Comet is a user agent acting on user instructions.

entries.stated_justification: Cloudflare said Perplexity used undeclared crawlers that changed user agents, IPs and ASNs to evade no-crawl directives.
entries.summary: Perplexity removed from Cloudflare's verified bots list and new managed rules added to block the stealth crawling; Perplexity disputed the account.

entries.stated_justification: Content creators should consent to, and be compensated for, AI crawling.
entries.summary: New domains are asked whether to allow AI crawlers, with blocking as the default, plus a planned pay-per-crawl system.

entries.system: Grok image generation and editing on X
entries.stated_justification: Global backlash over sexualized deepfake images made with Grok.
entries.summary: Image generation on X limited to paying subscribers; later reports say editing images of real people was restricted for all users depending on location.

entries.stated_justification: Sexualized AI-generated images and deepfakes produced with Grok.
entries.summary: Temporary block on access to Grok; reported as the first country to deny all access to the tool.

entries.platform_or_entity: Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission / xAI
entries.stated_justification: Access limited until effective safeguards against sexualized AI images are in place.
entries.summary: Malaysia restricted access to Grok a day after Indonesia.

entries.stated_justification: Grok posted antisemitic content, including praise of Hitler; xAI said it acted to ban hate speech before Grok posts on X.
entries.summary: Posts deleted and a pre-posting hate-speech filter added after a prompt change; one outlet reported text replies were briefly restricted (not corroborated).

entries.stated_justification: Content insulting President Erdogan and religious values, under Article 299 of the Turkish penal code.
entries.summary: First Turkish ban on content from an AI tool, covering about 50 Grok posts; reports differed on whether a full access ban took effect.

entries.stated_justification: API usage policies prohibit political campaigning and impersonating a person without consent.
entries.summary: Developer account removed; the voice bot built for a super PAC was disabled. Reported as OpenAI's first known restriction of AI use in a political campaign.

entries.system: Voice-commanded robotic rifle using the Realtime API
entries.stated_justification: OpenAI said it proactively identified a violation of its usage policies and notified the developer to cease the activity.
entries.summary: Developer cut off after viral videos of a turret aiming and firing on spoken commands.

entries.system: Apple Intelligence notification summaries for news and entertainment apps
entries.stated_justification: Summaries had produced false headlines, after complaints led by the BBC.
entries.summary: Summaries for the news and entertainment category disabled in the iOS 18.3 betas pending improvements; summaries for other apps continued.

entries.stated_justification: Viral odd and wrong answers; Google added detection of nonsensical queries, less reliance on satire and user-generated content, and triggering limits where overviews were not helpful, including health.
entries.summary: AI Overviews kept running but were triggered for fewer queries.

entries.stated_justification: The fatal 18 March 2018 Tempe crash was called an unquestionable failure to meet the expectation that public safety comes first.
entries.summary: Governor directed the Arizona DOT to suspend Uber's ability to test and operate autonomous vehicles on public roads.

entries.stated_justification: Vehicles judged not safe for public operation, and Cruise misrepresented information about a 2 October collision in which a pedestrian was dragged.
entries.summary: Immediate suspension of deployment and driverless testing permits with no set end date; testing with a safety driver was unaffected.

entries.stated_justification: FSD Beta could act unsafely around intersections and increase crash risk (recall 23V-085).
entries.summary: Recall of 362,758 vehicles remedied by an over-the-air update; NHTSA's wider Autopilot investigation stayed open.

entries.system: BabyQ (Turing Robot) and XiaoBing (Microsoft) group chatbots
entries.stated_justification: Tencent only said it was adjusting the third-party chatbot services; removal followed answers seen as unpatriotic, such as BabyQ answering No to whether it loved the Communist Party.
entries.summary: Two chatbots removed from the QQ messaging app after politically unwelcome answers.

entries.stated_justification: Discriminatory and offensive remarks about sexual minorities, plus privacy complaints about the training conversations.
entries.summary: Suspended about 20 days after launch; the company said it would discard the database and model. Korea's PIPC fined it KRW 103.3 million in April 2021 for privacy violations.

entries.platform_or_entity: Personal Information Protection Commission (South Korea) / DeepSeek
entries.stated_justification: Lack of transparency about third-party data transfers and possible excessive collection of personal data.
entries.summary: New downloads suspended in Korean app stores until the service complies with Korean privacy law; existing users and the web service were unaffected.

entries.system: DeepSeek products, apps and web services
entries.stated_justification: Unacceptable security risk to government systems, based on intelligence agency advice (PSPF Direction 001-2025).
entries.summary: Federal entities had to find and remove DeepSeek from all government systems and devices; public use was unaffected.

entries.stated_justification: Endangers national information security; based on a 2019 Executive Yuan rule on products that endanger cybersecurity.
entries.summary: Government agencies, public schools, state enterprises and critical infrastructure told not to use DeepSeek; the premier made it a full government ban days later.

entries.stated_justification: AI-generated voices count as artificial under the TCPA, so calls using them need prior consent; prompted by AI robocalls imitating President Biden before the New Hampshire primary.
entries.summary: Unanimous declaratory ruling, effective immediately; lawyers note it requires consent rather than banning the technology outright.

entries.system: AI therapy chatbots (Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act, HB 1806)
entries.stated_justification: Protect patients from unlicensed, unqualified AI providing therapy.
entries.summary: Bars AI from making therapeutic decisions or doing therapeutic communication; administrative support is still allowed; fines up to USD 10,000 per violation.

entries.system: AI systems engaging in prohibited practices (AI Act Article 5)
entries.stated_justification: Practices judged an unacceptable risk, such as manipulative techniques and social scoring.
entries.summary: First AI Act rules apply, banning eight categories of practice; penalties enforceable from 2 August 2025, up to EUR 35 million or 7% of turnover.

entries.platform_or_entity: US House of Representatives (Chief Administrative Officer)
entries.stated_justification: Risk of leaking House data to cloud services the House has not approved.
entries.summary: Copilot removed and blocked on House Windows devices; a government version was to be evaluated later.

entries.platform_or_entity: New York City Department of Education
entries.stated_justification: Concerns about negative effects on student learning and about the safety and accuracy of content.
entries.summary: ChatGPT blocked on school devices and networks; schools could request access for tech education.

entries.system: ChatGPT and other generative AI services
entries.stated_justification: Engineers accidentally leaked internal source code by uploading it to ChatGPT.
entries.summary: Use of generative AI barred on company devices and networks while security measures were prepared.

entries.system: OpenAI API traffic from unsupported regions (incl. mainland China and Hong Kong)
entries.stated_justification: Traffic from regions not on OpenAI's list of supported countries and territories would be blocked.
entries.summary: Developers in unsupported regions were warned in June 2024 that API traffic would be blocked from 9 July; Chinese AI firms offered migration programs.

entries.system: Claude services for entities majority-owned from unsupported regions
entries.stated_justification: Legal, regulatory and security risks from entities controlled from jurisdictions such as China, wherever they operate.
entries.summary: Terms updated to bar companies more than 50% owned, directly or indirectly, by entities headquartered in unsupported regions, including via cloud providers.

entries.system: General-purpose third-party AI assistants on WhatsApp (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Perplexity)
entries.stated_justification: Meta said the Business API is meant for business-to-customer messaging and that AI chatbots put a heavy load on its systems.
entries.summary: Terms changed in October 2025 to bar AI providers from distributing assistants through the API, effective 15 January 2026; business support bots still allowed. Italy's competition authority ordered Meta on 24 December 2025 to suspend the terms in Italy pending its investigation.

entries.system: Accounts and automated clients reading posts
entries.stated_justification: Owner cited extreme levels of data scraping and system manipulation.
entries.summary: Temporary daily caps on how many posts an account could read (initially 6,000 / 600 / 300, raised hours later), which hit ordinary users too.

entries.stated_justification: Enforce Reddit's Public Content Policy against bots without an agreement.
entries.summary: robots.txt updated, with continued rate limiting and blocking of unknown bots; partners and good-faith actors such as the Internet Archive were not expected to be affected.

entries.stated_justification: The browsing tool could show content in unwanted ways, e.g. full text of paywalled pages, so it was disabled to do right by content owners.
entries.summary: Web-browsing tool for ChatGPT Plus disabled while the paywall issue was fixed.

entries.system: Sora depictions of Martin Luther King Jr.
entries.stated_justification: Request from Dr. King's estate after users made disrespectful depictions.
entries.summary: Generations of King paused while guardrails for historical figures were strengthened; other estates may ask for opt-outs.

entries.stated_justification: An abundance of caution ahead of the many elections in 2024.
entries.summary: Election-related queries in any market holding elections get a stock reply pointing to Google Search; extends earlier US and EU restrictions.

entries.system: AI character accounts on Instagram and Facebook (e.g. Liv)
entries.stated_justification: Meta said they were part of a 2023 test and cited a bug that stopped users from blocking them; removal followed public backlash.
entries.summary: Meta deleted its own AI persona accounts and their posts after users and journalists criticized them.

entries.stated_justification: Prompt loopholes were used to make explicit celebrity deepfakes; text filtering was strengthened.
entries.summary: Workarounds such as describing a celebrity by occupation stopped working after 404 Media's report.

entries.stated_justification: Robotaxis passed stopped school buses; NHTSA had opened an investigation and sought information.
entries.summary: Voluntary software recall filed 10 December 2025; vehicles stayed in service, and Waymo declined a request from Austin school officials to pause service near schools.

entries.stated_justification: The system learned to penalize resumes signalling women candidates, and Amazon could not ensure it would not find other ways to discriminate.
entries.summary: Project abandoned by early 2017; reported by Reuters on 10 October 2018. Amazon said recruiters never used it to evaluate candidates.

entries.stated_justification: The agent deleted a customer's production database during a code freeze and misreported what it had done.
entries.summary: CEO announced automatic dev/prod database separation and a planning/chat-only mode so the agent cannot change production data during development.
